docs.title: Financial Reports: Scope, Navigation, Drill-Down, and Export

sections.text: Dynamic financial reports present interactive multi-level statements where every figure reflects your assigned access rights and posted transactions. A single operator configures reporting filters, navigates profit summaries and balance sheets, inspects supporting records, and exports data.

Before generating financial reports, verify access and configuration: - **User Role and Permissions**: Ensure your account has accounting reporting permissions. Dynamic reports compute figures using your assigned access rights; if you lack permission to view specific accounts or journals, the status line names what is excluded rather than showing an inaccurate silent zero. Reports never display journals or accounts you cannot access. - **Company Currency Consistency**: Monetary amounts appear without a currency symbol. When consolidating across companies, select entities that share the same company currency, or generate separate reports per company currency. - **Posted Journal Entries**: Reporting lines aggregate posted statutory journal items in the company currency. Unposted draft entries do not feed standard statements until posted.

1. Open reports directly from the Accounting app under **Accounting → Reporting** (such as **Profit and Loss**, **Balance Sheet**, **General Ledger**, or **Cash Flow Statement**). General dynamic report definitions also open from **Settings → Technical → Reporting → Dynamic Reports**. 2. Understand core statement roles: - **Profit and Loss**: Measures financial performance over a selected date range or fiscal period (incurred revenues and expenses). - **Balance Sheet**: Evaluates financial position at a specific date (cumulative assets, liabilities, and equity). - **General Ledger**: Displays detailed underlying journal items, posted debit/credit lines, and running balances for every account. 3. In the filter bar at the top of the report sheet, configure the scope: - **Companies**: Select the companies whose postings to include. At least one company must remain selected. Note that **Cash Flow Statement** requires running one company at a time. - **Period**: Choose a preset date range (**this or last month**, **quarter**, **year**, or **Today** for single-date snapshots). Select **Custom** to enter an exact start and end date. - **Compare**: Add comparison columns for the previous period, the same period last year, or a custom range. Specify the number of comparison periods and choose whether newest or oldest appears first. - **Options**: Select **Unfold all lines** to expand all levels, or choose **Hide zero rows** to omit accounts with zero balances while keeping folded groups accessible. - **General Ledger Opening**: In **General Ledger → Options**, select **Use fiscal-year opening** to read opening balances under the selected company's fiscal calendar within a single fiscal year. ![The Accounting dashboard groups transactions by journal. Open Reporting to inspect their combined results.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IndoERP/ERPForAll/a0b166f13a9bfef45efe154016c4f5d9fd2e37c0/.github/assets/accounting-dashboard.png)

Financial report sheets organize accounts hierarchically with interactive navigation and keyboard shortcuts: - **Unfolding Sections**: Click the chevron next to a section or account name, or select the line and press **Right**, to expand subordinate lines. Click the chevron again or press **Left** to fold the section. - **Paging Long Lists**: When a section has more rows than fit on one page, click **Show more** to load the remaining rows. Any loaded pages remain included when you return via breadcrumbs or export the statement. - **Sorting Columns**: Click a column header with a chevron to toggle sorting: largest first, smallest first, or report order. Only the main period sorts. - **Drilling into Transactions**: Click any amount to open its underlying journal items in a list view. Hovering over a line or focusing it reveals an arrow: click it to select **Records behind** for that column's entries, or **Open** to display the source master record in a form. - **Breadcrumb Navigation**: Return to the report using the breadcrumb. The view preserves your active filters, expanded rows, search queries, and loaded pages.

The Cash Flow Statement derives cash movements directly from posted statutory journal items affecting Bank and Cash accounts in company currency: - **Opening and Closing Balances**: Opening cash reflects Bank and Cash account balances prior to the first day of the period. Closing cash includes all postings through the period's final day. - **Reconciled Cash Flow Structure**: For example, in company USD: - Opening cash: 12,000 USD - Cash flows from operating activities: +5,000 USD - Cash flows from investing activities: −3,400 USD - Cash flows from financing activities: +5,000 USD - Closing cash balance: 18,600 USD (12,000 + 5,000 − 3,400 + 5,000 = 18,600 USD) - Unclassified cash movements: 0 USD - **Distinguishing Cash Movement Conditions**: - *No posted liquidity entry*: If no posted transactions affect Bank and Cash accounts during the period, net cash movement is zero and closing cash equals opening cash without generating cash activity rows. - *Zero net movement (Internal transfers)*: Direct fund transfers between two Bank and Cash accounts generate debit and credit liquidity postings that offset completely, resulting in net zero cash change. - *Mixed or conflicting cash-flow tags*: If counterpart lines carry multiple different tags, disagree across lines, or lack a tag, the entire transaction amount appears under **Unclassified cash movements** for operator review. - **Settlement Allocation**: Payments posted to an outstanding receipts/payments account appear once settled to a Bank or Cash account. The report does not allocate settlements back through reconciliation to the original customer invoice or vendor bill.

After setting filters and expanding target accounts, export the statement: 1. Review the status line directly beneath the filters to verify calculation time. Click **Refresh** if recent entries were posted while the report was open. 2. Click **PDF** to download a document, or **Print** to open the PDF in a new browser tab for printing. 3. Click **XLSX** to export a spreadsheet. Exports reproduce the active screen view, including date filters, company scope, expanded lines, and rows loaded via **Show more**.

- **Screen Limit Exceeded**: If expanding many rows or repeatedly clicking **Show more** exceeds the screen limit, the system stops expanding additional rows and keeps the last exportable table. - *Recovery*: Click the chevron on an open section to fold that group. Folding a group clears its cached subordinate pages, allowing you to unfold other target sections and re-export. - **Report Limit Refusal on Export**: If an export is refused due to total report size, an administrator can raise the limit in **Settings → Technical → Reporting → Dynamic Reports**. - **Fiscal Year Opening Reset**: Toggling **Use fiscal-year opening** in General Ledger automatically resets all expanded rows to folded. Unfold target lines again after changing this option.
